title: A path guard for protected folders must compare resolved paths, not raw text
rule: When a check refuses a user-given folder because it is or lies inside a protected folder (system font folders, the library folder, app data), compare resolved paths: refuse a path that is not absolute on the host (on Windows a root without a drive, `\Windows\Fonts`, is not), resolve `.` and `..`, drop the Windows `\\?\` prefix, and follow links on both sides (canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor, then append the parts that do not exist yet; `fm_platform::paths::resolve_links`). Test it with `..` on the way, a drive-less path, the verbatim prefix and a symlink to the protected folder.
rationale: E22.7 (#427): `is_within` compared path components as text, so a download folder `~/Documents/../.local/share/fonts`, `\Users\ada\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` or `\\?\C:\...` passed the rule-4 guard and the install would write into a folder the OS reads fonts from.
